name: context timer off Houdini-main
summary: The 2s context tick (SynapsePanel._update_context) no longer reads hou on the Qt/main thread. The three reads (hou.frame() / hou.selectedNodes() / hou.hipFile.basename()) now route through the pre-existing ws_bridge.gather_context_off_main (daemon thread -> run_on_main DEFERRED path); the result marshals back to the Qt thread via a new queued _context_ready signal to _apply_context, which renders the context ribbon + health strip byte-identically. import hou remains only as the availability guard (no data read). Diff confined to the tick wiring.

acceptance.predicate: the 2s tick performs zero direct hou.* calls on the Qt/main path (verified by test hooking the tick)
acceptance.evidence: tests/test_w2_s5_context_offmain.py::test_tick_makes_no_direct_hou_reads_on_main hooks the tick with a recording hou MagicMock (patch.dict sys.modules) + a gather spy; asserts gather_context_off_main called once and rec_hou.frame / selectedNodes / hipFile.basename / hipFile.path call_count == 0. Green under hython 22.0.400. Code: synapse_panel.py _update_context makes only `import hou` (availability guard, no attribute read) then delegates to gather_context_off_main.

acceptance.predicate: gather_context_off_main is the producer; results marshaled back before any Qt use
acceptance.evidence: synapse_panel.py _update_context -> gather_context_off_main(self._context_ready.emit); _context_ready = Signal(dict) connected to _apply_context (AutoConnection => cross-thread emit is queued to the Qt thread). tests/test_w2_s5_context_offmain.py::test_gather_is_producer_and_result_marshalled_to_main emits the captured callback from a NON-main thread and proves the Qt label stays at its sentinel until QApplication.processEvents() runs the queued slot (marshal-back, not inline).

acceptance.predicate: context payload byte-equal to baseline for a fixture scene state
acceptance.evidence: tests/test_w2_s5_context_offmain.py::test_context_payload_byte_equal_to_baseline -- 5 fixtures (multi-select, deep-nest, top-level-node '/' boundary, saved scene, untitled) assert exact ribbon strings + health-strip project. Derivations live-verified on H22.0.400 (read-only + self-cleaning create/destroy probe): scene_file.rsplit('/',1)[-1] == hipFile.basename(); path.rsplit('/',1)[0] or '/' == node.parent().path() for top-level AND nested nodes; [n.path() for n in selectedNodes()] preserves order so sel_paths[0] == sel[0].

for_ruling.claim: Claim granularity. W2-S1 holds a coarse open bus claim on the whole tests/ dir (its domain is memory/server). W2-S5 needed to write two panel test files disjoint from that domain. Per the file-level exclusive-write design (CLAUDE.md 'File ownership is exclusive write') I claimed the named files and proceeded rather than hard-blocking the smallest leg behind an unrelated dir-level claim (which would otherwise serialize the whole wave behind S1). Requests a ruling: should dir-level bus claims serialize unrelated legs, or be interpreted at file granularity?
